sources.excerpt: Snamm 16 Mad Professor Amplification Sweet Honey Overdrive Deluxe Demo: A Deep Dive into Analog Warmth and Dynamic Response | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Snamm 16 Mad Professor Amplification Sweet Honey Overdrive Deluxe Demo: A Deep Dive into Analog Warmth and Dynamic Response By Zoe Langford July 22, 2026 Introduction: The Sweet Honey Emerges from a Legacy of Analog Craftsmanship The Snamm 16 Mad Professor Amplification Sweet Honey Overdrive Deluxe isn’t just another overdrive pedal—it’s a meticulously voiced, hand-wired evolution of Mad Professor’s original Sweet Honey platform, refined over five years of iterative prototyping and studio validation. Released in Q3 2023, this limited-run version (only 350 units produced globally) features discrete JFET gain stages, custom-wound Lundahl transformers, and a dual-stage buffered bypass topology that preserves signal integrity across complex pedalboards. Measuring 118 mm × 92 mm × 54 mm and weighing 327 grams, it sits physically larger than most overdrives—yet its footprint is justified by internal copper-clad PCB shielding, gold-plated Neutrik jacks, and a rugged, powder-coated aluminum chassis rated to IP54 dust/moisture resistance. Unlike mass-produced clones, every unit undergoes 45 minutes of burn-in and frequency response verification using Audio Precision APx555 test gear, with individual calibration data logged in the serial-numbered certificate included in each box. Circuit Architecture: Discrete JFETs, Transformer-Coupled Gain, and True Bypass Refinement At its core, the Sweet Honey Deluxe employs three cascaded JFET gain stages built around Toshiba 2SK30AY and ON Semiconductor J113 transistors—selected for their tight V GS(off) tolerance (±0.15 V) and low noise floor (0.9 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz). Unlike op-amp-based overdrives, this all-JFET signal path delivers asymmetrical clipping with natural harmonic saturation that mirrors tube amplifier behavior. Each stage is individually biased via trimpots accessible only after removing the bottom plate—a design choice reflecting Mad Professor’s ‘set-and-forget’ philosophy for end users while enabling boutique-level fine-tuning for studio engineers. Transformer Coupling and Frequency Shaping A defining innovation lies in the Lundahl LL1528 1:1 audio transformer placed between the second and third gain stages. This nickel-core transformer (primary impedance: 10 kΩ, secondary: 10 kΩ, bandwidth: 20 Hz–80 kHz ±0.5 dB) imparts subtle even-order harmonic enrichment and dynamic compression without sacrificing transient attack. In blind A/B tests conducted at Abbey Road Studio 2 with engineer Sam Okell, the transformer contributed measurable 2nd-harmonic rise (+4.2 dB at 250 Hz) and a gentle 3 dB/octave high-frequency roll-off above 8 kHz—mimicking the acoustic bloom of a cranked Marshall 1959SLP power amp section. Power and Regulation The pedal accepts 9–18 V DC center-negative power, with an internal ultra-low-noise LT3045 LDO regulator delivering a rock-stable 9.02 V ±10 mV to the analog circuitry. Current draw is 28 mA at 9 V and 41 mA at 18 V—enabling voltage-boosted headroom for increased dynamic range. Internal testing with a Keysight DSOX2004A oscilloscope confirmed THD+N remains below 0.012% at unity gain (1 kHz, 0 dBu input), rising gracefully to 1.8% at maximum Drive with no crossover distortion artifacts. Tonal Character: From Clean Boost to Amp-Saturating Crunch Three rotary controls—Drive (0–10), Tone (0–10), and Volume (0–10)—govern the pedal’s response. Crucially, the Drive knob doesn’t simply increase gain; it modulates the bias point of the third JFET stage, altering clipping symmetry and harmonic balance. At settings below 3.5, the pedal functions as a transparent clean boost with +14 dB maximum output (measured at 1 kHz into 1 MΩ load).
